audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. The finite flat-current formula omits the initial offset; The step-limit kernel definition differs from the proof; The collision boundary rule lacks zeta inverse
limitations: Counterevidence and scope: Read the actual derivation5.38-5.39 and p61: delta factors persist, requiring product v^delta in C and w^delta in f. This validates necessary repairs, not every other normalization. Translation also changes the observed edge. Current differences between edges delta apart are bounded by delta via arc occupancy, so after sqrtL scaling no asymptotic counterexample follows. The exact finite-time Proposition5.4 used in the core flat derivation is false as stated and warrants Major.

Counterevidence and scope: Independently read Baik-Liu physical pp11-12: equations4.11-4.12 agree with the acquired paper proof. Unequal kernels do not alone establish unequal contour-integrated determinants. A local formula repair already in the proof suffices for this identified discrepancy; no corrected limit theorem falsity or complete steepest-descent certification claimed.

Counterevidence and scope: AppendixB.1 explicitly states and proves the corrected factor; zeta1 is unaffected. The sample w1,w2 are not asserted Bethe roots. Correcting the local rule removes the displayed obstruction without refuting the final eigenfunction statement.

Counterevidence and scope: The corrected root-unity statement applies to zeta^-N productw. Since |zeta|1, product|w|1 survives and is the actual quantity used in the subsequent size and small-z arguments. Generic-zeta exceptions remain intact; this does not refute their theorem at excluded parameters.

Counterevidence and scope: Remark2.5 provides no transformed generator/current formula. The check rules out ordinary complement/reflection as the asserted automatic extension, not every possible algebraic duality or a direct proof. At q0 TASEP the usual symmetry works. Full occupancy has no allowed generator move and needs separate treatment. Low-density formulas and fluctuation conclusions are not refuted.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
The state is an ordered configuration \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\) with \(0\leq x_1<\cdots<x_N<L\). Each particle attempts a right exclusion jump at rate \(p\), and a left push at rate \(q\), where \(p,q\geq0\) and \(p+q=1\). A left push moves the consecutive occupied block to the first hole. The total current \(Q\) counts all individual displacements; the local current \(Q_j\) counts net crossings of the edge \(j\to j+1\). The generator (2.8), page 9, rather than an alternative convention about attempted jumps, is used for every calculation in this report.

Equation reference: eq:conservation, eq:gauge. The deformation is \[g(Y,X;\zeta;t)=\mathbb E_Y[\zeta^{Q(t)}\mathbf1_{\{X(t)=X\}}],
 \qquad |\zeta|=1.\] An independently checked conservation law is \[
 Q(t)=\sum_i(x_i-y_i)+LQ_{L-1}(t).\] It holds at each allowed transition, including a push across the origin, and hence along every path. This verifies (3.25) and the gauge relation (3.30), pages 23–24. In particular, \[
 \zeta^L=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 g(Y,X;\zeta;t)=\zeta^{\sum_i(x_i-y_i)}
 \mathbb P_Y(X(t)=X).\] Exact rational enumeration also checked this transition identity and uniform stationarity on the rings \((L,N)=(6,2),(4,3),(3,1)\), comprising 76 allowed transitions at \(p=q=1/2\). These are finite-system checks, not a proof of all contour or asymptotic estimates.

The contour conditions on page 15 require \[\frac{1}{1-\rho}<\beta_1<\frac1\rho,\qquad
 \frac1\rho<\beta_2<\frac{L}{N-1},\qquad \rho=N/L,\] and thus \(2N<L\). Remark 4.4, page 39, supplies modified conditions at \(2N=L\). The generic spectral expansion explicitly excludes finitely many \(\zeta\)’s. Corollary 3.5, page 20, additionally assumes simple coupling roots at \(\zeta=1\); this review does not silently remove that assumption. Remark 4.7, page 41, distinguishes a fixed small contour from its limit as its radius tends to zero, resolving a possible apparent discontinuity in \(u_0\).
